The 2026 Draft: Quick Hits

Labor Day evening, Sept 7, 2026 · 15 rounds · 60 seconds per pick · 12 teams, snake format

  • The draft order came from an F1 race. Fantasy manager standings from the Dutch Grand Prix set the order top to bottom — Mike Gostlin's driver had the best finish, so he got the No. 1 overall pick. Jerome Prasad's driver (Pierre Gasly, P10) landed him at pick 9. Lucas Blair's driver didn't finish the race at all — dead last, pick 12.
  • Nobody's keeper cost crept into Round 1 — the earliest any keeper landed was Round 4 (Mac James, Josh Allen, in his second year as a keeper).
  • Five managers held onto a keeper for a second straight year, each at the discounted year-2 price the rule requires a round earlier than their original cost: Jerome Prasad (Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Round 6), Mac James (Josh Allen, Round 4), Jazz Dhillon (Brock Bowers, Round 7), Stuart Duncan (Ladd McConkey, Round 8), and Brad Harnum (Puka Nacua, Round 7).
  • The other seven managers kept a player for the first time this year, most at their original draft-round cost or the standard Round 9 default for a late-round or waiver pickup.
2026.1:
The Tobermory Telegraph — Week 1

Ringside coverage by S.S.C. Media — covering this league since it was founded, and not about to stop now.

Ladies and gentlemen, lace up. Week 1 is in the books, and wouldn't you know it — the schedule-makers front-loaded us a Rivalry Week right out of the gate. Six grudges, six tilts, one telegraph. And it came during a real slugfest of an opening weekend around the league — the Bengals' rebuilt defense forced four turnovers to steal one from Tampa, the Lions needed overtime just to survive New Orleans blowing a 21-0 lead, and the Bills-Texans game came down to the final possession. Let's get into our own six — and the box score has some real stories in it this week.

THE PERFECT WEEK. Mike Gostlin didn't just beat Ben Matsumoto Sunday — he set the single best possible lineup he could have set, and Sleeper's own math confirms it: 195.04 points, every one of them the maximum available to him. League's highest score, league's best-managed roster, 41% over his own projection. Credit where it's due — Jalen Coker went off for him, 8 catches, 138 yards, 2 scores, the best individual weekend any starter turned in across the whole league. Small mercy for Ben: his own Javonte Williams punched in a real touchdown for Dallas this week. Didn't matter — the Cowboys lost anyway, and so did Ben, 146.96 to a perfect game. That's not a rivalry loss, Ben, that's a receipt with a stamp on it — and it's the exact receipt Ben himself handed Mike last year, when he beat him in this same matchup. Even now.

THE HARD-LUCK CASE OF THE WEEK. Somebody has to lose the game nobody deserved to lose, and this week it was Ian Singh. His starting lineup alone produced the league's best quarterback (Caleb Williams, 37.26 points) and the league's best running back (Derrick Henry, 35.3 points on 3 touchdowns) — and his bench still had gas left in the tank, with both the league's best benched quarterback (Trevor Lawrence, 26.1 points) and best benched wideout (Devaughn Vele, 19.9) sitting there doing nothing for him. Four of the best individual performances anywhere in the league, on one roster, and Ian still dropped his game to Josh Dass, 165.80–155.96. Fantasy football owes you one, Ian.

KEEPER FOOTNOTE. Josh's real value play this week wasn't loud, but it was real: Zay Flowers, kept into 2026 at a Round 5 price, went 5 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown — all of it in the first half, before a hamstring injury ended his day early. That came in the Ravens' 41-23 win over Indianapolis. Funny enough, the other side of that same game has a Tobermory tie too: Jonathan Taylor, a name Josh once drafted back in 2025 but didn't keep, resurfaced fresh in the actual 2026 draft on Mac James's roster instead — and turned in 2 touchdowns and 98 yards of his own, on the losing side. Same Sunday, same game, two Tobermory managers, opposite results.

NOT MUCH BETTER. Jerome Prasad put a real beating on Lucas Blair, 127.66–91.16. Lucas didn't just lose — he missed his own projection by 25%, the worst under-performance of the week. Rough way to open a telegraph column, but the numbers don't lie. This is the longest-running rivalry in the league, 31 meetings dating back to 2012, and Lucas still holds the edge all-time — but Jerome's won this one two years running now, and Sunday made it official. Jerome, for what it's worth, got a genuine league-best performance of his own: his Steelers defense was the top defensive unit in the whole league this week — 2 interceptions, a defensive touchdown, 4 sacks.

SOLID, NOT SPECTACULAR. Gurminder Kambo handled Stuart Duncan, 139.82–118.70 — though he left a genuine league-best bench performance on the table doing it (Kyle Monangai, 20.4 points, didn't dress). Mac James did the same to Brad Harnum, 121.46–105.82 — and that's back-to-back wins in this rivalry for Mac, enough to pull the all-time series dead even. Mac's got real bragging rights to back it up now, twice over. His year-two keeper Josh Allen put on a show Sunday: four total touchdowns, a game-winning strike with 1:36 left, a win over a Houston defense that's given him fits for years. And as covered above, he's also got Jonathan Taylor's two-touchdown day to his name this week. Small consolation for Brad: Trey McBride was the league's best tight end this week, 9 catches, 95 yards, a score. Business, not personal. This time.

THE NAIL-BITER, WITH AN ASTERISK. Save the best for last: Jazz Dhillon over Romie Jassal, 124.00–119.40. A 4.6-point margin in a rivalry game — that's the stuff. But here's the sting: Sleeper's own numbers say Romie set the single worst-managed lineup in the league this week, leaving points on his own bench he never should have. A win was sitting right there. Small silver lining — his Evan McPherson was the league's best kicker, 19 points on four field goals. Doesn't soften the loss much, Romie, but it's something.

2026.2:
The Tobermory Telegraph — Week 2

Ringside coverage by S.S.C. Media — covering this league since it was founded, and not about to stop now.

Three teams are still unbeaten heading into Week 3, and two of them had the kind of week that makes the other ten a little nervous. Let's get into it.

THE HEADLINER. Jerome Prasad put up the week's highest score, 173.98, beating Mike Gostlin 173.98–133.48 and clearing his own projection by 30% while he was at it. The engine behind it: Jaxon Smith-Njigba — the same JSN kept into year two at a Round 6 price — went for 9 catches, 155 yards, 3 touchdowns, the best individual wide receiver performance in the league this week. Travis Kelce chipped in the league's best tight end line too, 9 catches, 101 yards, a score. Two league-best starters on one roster, in the same week. That win also pulls Jerome ahead in the all-time series with Mike, 12 wins to 10.

NOT TO BE OUTDONE. Mac James is also 2-0, and his roster had a week almost as loud as Jerome's. Josh Allen — Mac's actual keeper — put up 40.82 points, the league's best quarterback performance, easily topping his own big Week 1 game. Jonathan Taylor added the league's best running back line on top of it, 24 carries, 92 yards, 2 touchdowns, plus work in the passing game. A third league-best starter, Brandon Aubrey at kicker, rounded it out. Three positional bests on one roster is not a normal fantasy week. Mac beat Jazz Dhillon 156.42–108.28, extending his own series lead there to 16 wins to 10.

THE MASSACRE. Gurminder Kambo set the closest thing to a perfect lineup a manager can set this year — 99% of his own maximum possible score, Sleeper's math says — and it showed: 165.76–63.84, a 102-point demolition of Josh Dass. On the other side of that game, Josh had the exact opposite week: worst-managed lineup in the league (68% of his own ceiling), the lowest score of anyone, and a projection missed by 46%. Rough night all around for Josh — even his best bench running back, Rachaad White, only would have added another 14 points to a lineup that needed a lot more than that. That result also pushes a genuinely close all-time series, Gurminder over Josh, to 14 wins to 12 — not much separation left there, this week's score aside.

THE ONE THAT CAME DOWN TO THE WIRE. Romie Jassal held off Ian Singh 115.78–112.22, a 3.6-point margin, the closest game of the week by a wide stretch. Extends Romie's own series lead over Ian to 12 wins to 8.

THE UPSET. Lucas Blair doesn't have Brad Harnum's number in this rivalry — Brad leads that all-time series 12 games to 5 — but Sunday wasn't one of Brad's, and Lucas took full advantage, 115.70–94.42. Wins over Brad have been rare for Lucas; worth flagging when one actually happens.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING. Stuart Duncan beat Ben Matsumoto 130.66–117.38, and did it behind the league's best defense — Minnesota held opponents to 3 points and forced a turnover on top of it, 15 points from a unit most managers overlook. Small footnote: George Kittle was the league's best benched tight end this week, and he was sitting on Stuart's own bench the whole time.

Live standings and Power Rankings both reflect what happened on the field — check the Current Season and Stats tabs for the full picture. Until next week.
2026.3:
The Tobermory Telegraph — Week 3

Ringside coverage by S.S.C. Media — covering this league since it was founded, and not about to stop now.

Three weeks in, the card has a clear main event and a clear undercard. One team is still unbeaten, one is still looking for its first win, two favourites hit the canvas, and one manager did everything right and still lost. Let's get into it.

THE CRUELEST NIGHT IN THE LEAGUE. Stuart Duncan set the perfect lineup this week — Sleeper's own math says every available point was scored: 152.64. It wasn't enough. Mike Gostlin won 153.54–152.64, a 0.90-point decision, the narrowest result of the week by a mile. The difference-maker was Jahmyr Gibbs, the league's best running back this week: 20 carries, 99 yards, 2 touchdowns on the ground, plus 7 catches for 65 yards and a third score, in a 31–24 Detroit win over the Jets. Stuart did nothing wrong. Stuart's Minnesota defense was the league's best for the second straight week (2 interceptions, 6 sacks and a touchdown in a 23–16 win at Tampa Bay), and George Kittle added 26.2 from the tight end spot. Sometimes a fighter lands every punch thrown and still loses on the cards. That's this one. Mike's all-time edge in the series grows to 13–5.

STILL UNDEFEATED. Jerome Prasad is the last unbeaten team standing at 3–0 after beating Brad Harnum 157.46–129.88. Jaxon Smith-Njigba — kept into year two at a Round 6 price — was the league's best wide receiver for the second week running: 10 catches on 14 targets, 128 yards, 2 touchdowns, and for good measure a 14-yard completion on the only pass attempt of the day. All of it came in a 33–31 Seattle loss in Washington — the fantasy points count the same either way. The lineup call that mattered: Tyler Shough got the start at quarterback and put up 23.8, while Joe Burrow sat on the bench with 22.58 — the best benched quarterback in the league, and still the right decision by a hair. For Brad, it's 0–3, the only winless team left. Harold Fannin chipped in 24.1 at tight end, and Kalif Raymond scored 21 on Brad's bench — the best benched receiver in the league. Brad still leads this all-time series, 11–9, but the gap is closing.

THE HIGH-WATER MARK. Jazz Dhillon put up the week's highest score, 176.30, beating the projection by 40% and Lucas Blair 176.30–135.84. Brock Bowers — Jazz's year-two keeper — was the league's best tight end: 10 catches on 13 targets, 116 yards, a touchdown, in a 35–27 Raiders win in New Orleans. Bijan Robinson added 35.3 in Atlanta's 35–14 rout at Green Bay and Michael Wilson 25.9 out of the flex. The hard-luck note belongs to Lucas: 135.84 was the fifth-highest score of the week, with Drake London (28.4) and Garrett Wilson (26.7) both delivering, and Lucas still lost by 40. Wrong opponent, wrong week. Jazz now leads the series 12–8.

THE BLOWOUT. Ben Matsumoto got a first win of the season and made it emphatic: 125.94–81.64 over Josh Dass, the week's biggest margin at 54%. Nobody on Ben's side needed to be a hero — Jaylen Warren (20.6), Luther Burden (19.8) and Chris Olave (19.7) just kept landing jabs. Josh's night went the other way: Justin Jefferson managed 5.2 points in the lineup while Wan'Dale Robinson scored 18.7 on the bench. Josh still leads this series, but only 9–7 now.

THE UPSETS. The scoreboard's new betting lines made their debut this week, and the favourites went 4 for 6. The two that didn't hold:

Mac James was an 8.5-point favourite over Ian Singh and lost 111.48–79.26. Sleeper's report doesn't pull punches: the lowest score in the league, a projection missed by 41%, and the worst-managed lineup of the week — only 79% of what the best possible lineup would have scored. Miami scored 10 points all day against Kansas City, which goes a long way toward explaining De'Von Achane (1.7) and Jaylen Waddle (6.4); Khalil Shakir (1.6) barely registered either, Jonathan Taylor managed 9.2, and the Denver defense scored 14 on Mac's bench — the best benched defense in the league — while Carolina's started and put up 4. Ian didn't need anything fancy: Derrick Henry (21.9) and Kenneth Walker (21.3) did the heavy lifting, and Chase McLaughlin was the league's best kicker with 12. Ian's series lead grows to 10–7.

Gurminder Kambo was a 9-point favourite over Romie Jassal and lost 126.58–106.02. Brock Purdy was the league's best quarterback for Romie: 297 passing yards and 4 touchdowns, 31.28 points, in a 36–30 San Francisco win over Arizona. Ja'Marr Chase added 24.8. The remarkable part is how much Romie left on the bench and still won going away — Juwan Johnson scored 23.3 there, the best benched tight end in the league (in the same Raiders–Saints game as Jazz's Bowers), with Terry McLaurin adding another 19.7. Gurminder's Philadelphia defense scored zero in a 27–7 loss in Chicago. Romie now leads the longest-running series on this week's card, 14–11.

2026.4:
The Tobermory Telegraph — Week 4

Ringside coverage by S.S.C. Media — covering this league since it was founded, and not about to stop now.

The last unbeaten record in the league fell this week, three teams now share the top at 3–1, and Brad Harnum is still waiting on a first win. Oddest stat of the week: the two best quarterback scores on any Tobermory roster both came off the bench — Brad's Drake Maye (26.16) and Jerome's Joe Burrow (23.7) each outscored every quarterback who actually started. Let's get into it.

THE STREAK SNAPS. Stuart Duncan ended Jerome Prasad's perfect start, 155.20–136.64, as the bigger underdog of the week's two upsets. Kyren Williams was the league's best running back: 16 carries, 80 yards, 2 touchdowns, plus 10 catches for 67 yards, in the Rams' 24–20 win in Philadelphia. Jake Bates was the league's best kicker, 4 for 4 on field goals with one from beyond 50, and Malik Nabers added 23.2 in the Giants' 36–24 win over Arizona — enough to cover for keeper Ladd McConkey's zero. Jerome had the week's second-biggest individual score in CeeDee Lamb, 41.3 points in Dallas's 34–30 shootout win in Houston, and still came up short. The difference was sitting on Jerome's bench. Last week the Tyler Shough-over-Joe Burrow call was right by a hair; this week Burrow outscored Shough by 7.8, and Alvin Kamara (22.8) sat while Jeremiyah Love (6.5) started. Those two swaps alone would have won it. Jerome still owns this series, 15–5, but Stuart picked a good night to take one.

THE MAIN EVENT. Ben Matsumoto set a near-perfect lineup — 99% of the best possible score, Sleeper's math says — and posted the week's highest total, 186.42, beating the projection by a third. The knockout punch was Tetairoa McMillan, the league's best wide receiver: 14 catches on 16 targets, 192 yards, 2 touchdowns, in Carolina's 32–26 win over Detroit. Javonte Williams — Ben's Round 9 keeper — added 31.3 in Dallas's win over Houston. Romie Jassal got 30.8 from Nico Collins on the losing side of Dallas–Houston and not much else: Ja'Marr Chase 5.7, keeper Blake Corum 3.1. Final: 186.42–105.52, an 81-point margin, the biggest of the week. Ben has now climbed back to 2–2 after an 0–2 start. Romie still leads their series 13–7.

THE ROUGH ONE. Gurminder Kambo had the week's lowest score, 71.24, and Sleeper's report doesn't sugarcoat how: the worst-managed lineup in the league, only 66% of what the best possible lineup would have scored, and a projection missed by a third. Marcus Mariota started at quarterback and managed 5.3 in Washington's 30–13 loss to Indianapolis, while Jalen Hurts sat on the bench with 13.5. The bigger miss: Kyle Monangai, the best benched running back in the league, ran 30 times for 146 yards and 2 touchdowns in Chicago's 23–12 win over the Jets — 28 points, never used. In fairness, even the perfect version of this lineup (108.52) wouldn't have caught Mac James, who won 143.62–71.24 behind Chuba Hubbard (25.9), Romeo Doubs (23.8) and Jonathan Taylor (22.7). Mac moves to 3–1 and stretches the series lead over Gurminder to 10–5.

THE NAIL-BITER. Josh Dass beat Mike Gostlin 128.16–121.90, the closest game of the week and the other big upset on the card. Bryce Young was the league's best starting quarterback — 29 of 41, 329 yards, 2 touchdowns — in the same Carolina win that made McMillan's day, and keeper Zay Flowers added 25.8 in Baltimore's 24–18 win over Tennessee. Mike got 27 points from Emanuel Wilson but a zero from Rashee Rice, and Jared Goff's 20.5 on the bench would only have closed 3.5 of the 6.26-point gap. That result puts this rivalry exactly level: 11 wins apiece, 22 meetings.

ALSO ON THE CARD. Jazz Dhillon beat Brad Harnum 162.48–126.98 to join the 3–1 club, with Bijan Robinson (27.7 in Atlanta's 45–24 rout in New Orleans), Tee Higgins (26.7) and Quinshon Judkins (21.6) leading the way. Brad got 27.7 from keeper Puka Nacua, but the cruel part is the quarterback spot: Drake Maye scored 26.16 on Brad's bench in New England's 29–26 win at Buffalo while Jordan Love started and put up 13.1. Even with Maye in, it wouldn't have been enough — Brad is 0–4, though Brad still leads this series 13–9. And Ian Singh beat Lucas Blair 131.68–123.28 behind 30.9 from Kenneth Walker, despite Lucas starting the league's best tight end (Sam LaPorta, 22.4) and best defense (Seattle: 2 interceptions, 4 sacks, 2 fumble recoveries in a 30–23 win over the Chargers). Lucas falls to 1–3 but still leads that series 12–9.

BY THE NUMBERS. The scoreboard's betting lines went 4 for 6 for the second straight week; both misses came on favourites of more than two touchdowns — Jerome and Mike.

Live standings, Power Rankings and the head-to-head records above all include this week's results — check the Current Season and Stats tabs for the full picture. Until next week.
2026.5:
The Tobermory Telegraph — Week 5

Ringside coverage by S.S.C. Media — covering this league since it was founded, and not about to stop now.

The winless streak is over, and it ended loudly. Jazz Dhillon is alone at the top at 4–1, six teams are bunched at 3–2, and the Power Rankings have a new No. 1. All of it in a week with Kansas City and Carolina on bye, which emptied a few lineups before kickoff. Let's get into it.

THE BREAKOUT. Brad Harnum came into Week 5 at 0–4 and left with the highest score of the 2026 season: 218.96, a 123-point demolition of Ian Singh (218.96–95.74), beating the projection by 53%. Last week Brad benched Drake Maye for Jordan Love and watched Maye outscore every starting quarterback in the league. This week Brad flipped it, and Maye was the league's best quarterback: 26 of 34, 374 yards, 4 touchdowns, plus a rushing score, in New England's 45–17 rout of Las Vegas. (Love scored 25.28 on the bench — the best benched quarterback in the league — so this time both choices would have worked.) Keeper Puka Nacua was the league's best receiver, 17 catches on 24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown in the Rams' overtime loss to Buffalo, Bucky Irving added 31.5, George Pickens 28.0, and the Houston defense was the league's best, holding Tennessee to 3 points. Ian's night was the opposite: the lowest score of the week, the worst-managed lineup (81% of the best possible), and an Indianapolis defense that scored zero. Ian's kicker, Spencer Shrader, was the league's best at the position (5 for 5), which tells you how the rest of it went. Ian still leads this series 15–11. Brad is 1–4, and the hole is real — but off the canvas at last.

THE PERFECT GAME. Mike Gostlin set the perfect lineup — every available point, 176.44 of them — and beat Romie Jassal 176.44–119.96. With Patrick Mahomes on bye, Mike went to Jared Goff (28.9) alongside Goff's Detroit teammate Jahmyr Gibbs, who was the league's best running back for the second time this season: 25 carries, 151 yards, 2 touchdowns, plus 5 catches for 56 yards, in Detroit's 45–21 win in Arizona. Christian Watson added 32.3 in Green Bay's 31–7 win over Chicago. That's 3–2 with the most points in the league, and Mike is the new No. 1 in the Power Rankings. Romie got 26.3 from Mike Evans and left 20.9 from C.J. Stroud on the bench. Romie still leads this series 11–7.

TOP OF THE TABLE. Jazz Dhillon beat Jerome Prasad 116.80–99.10, the closest game of the week, in a matchup the scoreboard's lines had as a pick'em. Matthew Stafford (27.3, in the Rams' overtime loss) and Brock Bowers (23.0) carried Jazz to 4–1, alone in first. Jerome finally started Joe Burrow, who delivered 24.6 in Cincinnati's 31–24 win in Miami — and then most of the rest of the lineup disappeared: CeeDee Lamb 2.9 in Dallas's loss to Tampa Bay, Jeremiyah Love 2.2, Carnell Tate 1.6, with Travis Kelce on bye. Sleeper had Jerome projected for 137.4 and the lineup missed by 28%. Two straight losses after a 3–0 start. Jerome still leads the series 11–7.

ALL SQUARE. Stuart Duncan beat Josh Dass 170.94–142.56 behind Parker Washington (30.4, in Jacksonville's 19–17 win over Philadelphia) and Malik Nabers (29.1). Josh had the league's best tight end in Isaiah Likely (11 catches on 13 targets, 94 yards, 2 touchdowns) and 32.3 from Jayden Daniels — and both played in the same game as Nabers, a Giants–Commanders matchup that ended 27–27 in overtime. Fitting, because this series is now dead level too: 13 wins apiece over 26 meetings. That's two all-time rivalries knotted up in two weeks.

THE REDEMPTION. One week after starting Marcus Mariota over Jalen Hurts, Gurminder Kambo started Jacoby Brissett over Hurts — and this time the call was right by 12 points. Brissett put up 25.3, James Cook 22.8, Davante Adams 22.1, and Gurminder beat Lucas Blair 149.08–105.82 as a slight underdog: the only favourite to lose on the card this week. Lucas got 19.8 from Sam LaPorta but 7.9 from Bo Nix, and the Denver backfield bit back: RJ Harvey started and scored 0.7, while J.K. Dobbins scored 15.4 on the bench. Lucas falls to 1–4 but still leads this series 11–8.

ALSO ON THE CARD. Ben Matsumoto beat Mac James 121.00–102.80 for a third straight win after an 0–2 start, led by Jaylen Warren's 36.8 in Pittsburgh's 34–22 win over Indianapolis. Mac got 30.5 from Josh Allen in Buffalo's overtime win over the Rams, but Brian Thomas scored zero and Romeo Doubs 2.6. Ben leads this series 14–8.

BY THE NUMBERS. The scoreboard's lines went 5 for 6, the best week yet; the only miss was the near coin flip in Gurminder–Lucas. The standings: Jazz 4–1; Mike, Stuart, Ben, Jerome, Gurminder and Mac all 3–2; Ian, Romie and Josh 2–3; Brad and Lucas 1–4.

Live standings, Power Rankings and the head-to-head records above all include this week's results — check the Current Season and Stats tabs for the full picture. Until next week.
2026.6:
The Tobermory Telegraph — Week 6

Ringside coverage by S.S.C. Media — covering this league since it was founded, and not about to stop now.

Nobody is alone at the top anymore. Six teams are bunched at 4–2, the Power Rankings have a new No. 1 for the second week running, and for the first time this season the scoreboard's lines were saved in advance — locked in Sunday morning before the 1 PM kickoffs, with Thursday's game already played and London under way. The favourites went 4 for 6, and the two that fell went down hard. Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota were on bye. Let's get into it.

THE KNOCKOUT. Brad Harnum went into Week 6 as a 17.5-point favourite, given a 71% chance by the lines. Gurminder Kambo put up the week's highest score and won 159.72–121.10, the biggest margin of the week and the biggest upset on the card. Gurminder beat the projection by 30%: Bhayshul Tuten 24.7, James Cook 24.3 in Buffalo's 33–30 win in Las Vegas, DeVonta Smith 20.5, and the Kansas City defense was the league's best (an interception, four sacks, a forced fumble and a recovery, and just 6 points allowed in a 22–6 win over the Chargers). Gurminder also collected two benchwarmer awards for a combined 3.1 points, which is the kind of trophy nobody puts on the mantel. Brad started Drake Maye over Jordan Love and was right again (23.8 to 20.2), but Germie Bernard scored 25.7 on the bench in Pittsburgh's overtime win at Tampa Bay, and the Houston defense managed 1 point in a 34–31 shootout in London. Brad has the fifth-most points in the league and a 1–5 record. Gurminder leads this series 12–10.

THE PERFECT LOSS. For the second week running, Mike Gostlin set the perfect lineup — and this time every available point added up to 92.48. Patrick Mahomes managed 10.5 in Kansas City's 22–6 win, Kyle Pitts led the team with 23.0, and the bench had nothing to give: Rashee Rice and Tyler Warren scored zero and Jared Goff was on bye. Mac James won 123.90–92.48 as a 19-point favourite, with Jonathan Taylor 21.1, Chuba Hubbard 19.1 in Carolina's 25–14 win in Philadelphia, Josh Allen 18.3, and 13.0 from a Denver defense that won 17–14 in overtime on Thursday. Mike still has the most points in the league but slips four places to No. 5 in the Power Rankings at 3–3. And that's another all-time rivalry dead level: Mac and Mike are 11–11.

BACK ON TOP. With Joe Burrow on bye, Jerome Prasad went to Tyler Shough, who scored 27.0 in New Orleans' 34–27 win over the Giants, and Jerome beat Josh Dass 155.36–124.74, covering a 17-point line with room to spare. Jaxon Smith-Njigba added 25.4, DK Metcalf 20.3 and Carnell Tate 19.0 in Tennessee's 26–20 win in Indianapolis. Josh had the league's best tight end for the second week in a row — Isaiah Likely, 6 catches for 99 yards, a touchdown and a two-point conversion — and started Bryce Young (19.8) over Jayden Daniels, who scored 21.0 on the bench. Jerome is 4–2, jumps four places to No. 1 in the Power Rankings, and now leads this series 15–3. Josh falls to 2–4.

THE UPSET. Ian Singh set the worst lineup of the week — 82% of the best possible, with Caleb Williams (16.5) and Keenan Allen (16.2) on the bench while Cam Skattebo (0.0) and MarShawn Lloyd (1.0) started — and won anyway. Trevor Lawrence was the league's best quarterback: 24 of 41, 306 yards, 4 touchdowns, in Jacksonville's 34–31 loss to Houston in London. Kenneth Walker added 27.9. Jazz Dhillon was an 11-point favourite and missed the projection by 27%: Bijan Robinson 7.3, Matthew Stafford 16.9 in the Rams' 18–16 loss to Arizona, and Harrison Butker, the league's best kicker (three field goals, one from 50-plus), couldn't make up the rest. Ian won 106.54–97.18, the closest game of the week. Jazz's three-game winning streak is over, and so is the solo lead: down four places to No. 6. Ian leads this series 11–8.

THE CLIMBER. Stuart Duncan beat Romie Jassal 120.32–90.06 for a third straight win. Christian McCaffrey was the league's best running back (two touchdowns, 9 catches on 10 targets) in San Francisco's 23–17 win over Washington on Monday night, and Malik Nabers was the best receiver: 12 catches on 15 targets for 165 yards, in the Giants' loss to New Orleans. The benchwarmer award for defenses went to Stuart's Minnesota Vikings, with zero points, on account of being on bye. Romie started Dameon Pierce (15.0) and left Blake Corum's 14.0 and a touchdown on the bench. Stuart is 4–2 and up to No. 2 in the Power Rankings, but Romie still leads this series 10–9. Romie has lost three straight.

ALSO ON THE CARD. Ben Matsumoto beat Lucas Blair 111.42–89.68 for a fourth straight win after an 0–2 start, the longest active winning streak in the league. It could have been more: Tre Tucker scored 26.7 on Ben's bench (5 catches, 97 yards, 2 touchdowns in the Raiders' 33–30 loss to Buffalo). Lucas had the lowest score of the week and started four Broncos — Bo Nix (4.5), RJ Harvey (14.6), J.K.
